entries.text: Customers say checkout felt slow in Europe this morning, but no alert fired. Use the Cisco Deep Time Series Model to check the last 24 hours of checkout latency for anomalies in each region.
I'll load the Splunk and CDTSM skills, then search the last 24 hours of checkout latency by region.
Splunk MCP is ready. Next I’ll inspect `splunk_run_query` and find checkout latency fields so CDTSM can run per region.

args.query: checkout service request logs latency by region

entries.text: Data-source discovery failed, so I’ll list indexes and sourcetypes and sample checkout events directly.
Checkout logs are `sourcetype=checkout`. I’ll sample fields, then run CDTSM on p95 latency by region for the last 24 hours.

args.query: sourcetype=checkout | stats count by region | sort -count
index=* sourcetype=checkout | stats count by index, sourcetype
index=demo_checkout sourcetype=checkout | fieldsummary maxvals=10 | table field, count, values

entries.text: Checkout data is in `index=demo_checkout` with `latency_ms` and `region`. Running CDTSM anomaly detection on 5-minute p95 per region.

args.query: index=demo_checkout sourcetype=checkout | bin _time span=5m | stats perc95(latency_ms) AS p95 by _time region | apply CDTSM p95 BY region mode=anomaly detection_window_earliest=-8h | eval is_anom=if('_isAnomaly.p95'=1,1,0) | eval peak_ratio=if(is_anom=1,p95/'p95.forecast',null()) | stats sum(is_anom) AS anomalous_points, min(eval(if(is_anom=1,_time,null()))) AS first_anom, max(eval(if(is_anom=1,_time,null()))) AS last_anom, max(eval(if(is_anom=1,p95,null()))) AS peak_p95, max(peak_ratio) AS peak_vs_forecast by region | eval first_anom=strftime(first_anom,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval last_anom=strftime(last_anom,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") | eval peak_p95=round(peak_p95,1) | eval peak_vs_forecast=round(peak_vs_forecast,2) | table region, anomalous_points, first_anom, last_anom, peak_p95, peak_vs_forecast | sort -anomalous_points

entries.text:
**CDTSM found a Europe-only latency anomaly this morning.** Other regions stayed normal, which is why a global or US-centric alert would have stayed quiet.

| Region | Anomalous 5-min points | Window (UTC) | Peak p95 (ms) | Peak vs forecast |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| eu-west-1 | 27 | 2026-11-18 05:45 – 07:55 | 1535.2 | 4.63× |
| us-east-1 | 0 | — | — | — |
| us-west-2 | 0 | — | — | — |
| ap-southeast-1 | 0 | — | — | — |

Checkout p95 in `eu-west-1` ran about **4.6× above the model forecast** for roughly two hours (05:45–07:55 UTC, morning in Europe). US and APAC series had no CDTSM anomaly flags in the last 24 hours.
Make that an alert called demo_checkout_latency_anomaly: run it every 15 minutes and fire when the model flags a latency anomaly in any region.
I'll look up `saved-search add` parameters, then create `demo_checkout_latency_anomaly` without `--yes` so we can confirm it.
